title: SIG questionnaire walkthrough - Cosmos Payments
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Cosmos Payments through the standard SIG questionnaire responses and supporting evidence. Primary topics: SOC 2 scope, data residency, KMS/encryption, SSO/SCIM and RBAC, audit log retention, and evidence artifacts. Customer requested specific artifacts (SOC 2 report, network diagram, KMS key policy) and a follow-up technical deep dive to validate private deployment options. Next steps agreed: send completed SIG export, SOC 2 report, KMS sample policies, schedule technical deep dive and provide an example network segmentation diagram.

transcript:
Header: 2026-06-10 16:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood CSM), Marcus (Cosmos Head of IT), Priya (Cosmos SecEng), Samir (Procurement), Elena (Legal)

Summary: quick SIG walkthrough focused on encryption/KMS, SOC2 scope, RBAC/SSO, and evidence items. transcript follows, auto timestamps approximate. transcription quality medium, some words garbled.

0:00 Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll kick off, I'm Aisha from Redwood Inference, joined by Jonas our solutions engineer and Lina our CSM. Marcus: yep thanks, appreciate you fitting this in.
0:22 Jonas: Quick agenda — walk through your SIG, call out where we usually land on answers, point to the artifacts we can provide, and note any gaps you want us to fill.
1:05 Priya: Great, main things for us are encryption/KMS integration and data residency. also SOC 2 evidence — we need to see control mapping.
1:30 Jonas: For SOC 2 we maintain a Type II report and a controls matrix. we can redac certain customer-specific bits but the report covers platform controls (security, availability).
2:00 Marcus: Is it full stack? like does Redwood include the private deploy package in SOC2 scope?
2:20 Jonas: short answer: hosted platform and control plane are in scope; private deployments customers run on-prem need a different appendix. we do have guidance and checklists for private installs; some controls are shared responsibility.
3:05 Elena: We need to understand if any customer PII is processed in logs or S3 that Redwood controls. Data residency wise we are constrained to US and EU.
3:40 Aisha: Yes, by default customer data for hosted is stored in region chosen; we support regional tenancy and can provide data residency commitments. For private deployment you'd keep everything in your VPC.
4:10 Priya: How about encryption keys — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS/HSM?
4:35 Jonas: We support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. For hosted we offer Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) integrations with AWS KMS and can discuss HSM options. We can share example key policies and the KMS flow.
5:15 Samir: Procurement question — can we get sample contract language around key custody and access?
5:30 Aisha: yes we'll include sample wording.
6:00 Jonas: On RBAC and SSO — we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM user provisioning, role-based access control with customizable roles and audit trails.
6:40 Priya: Do you log admin actions and provide immutable audit logs?
7:00 Jonas: We capture admin events, API access, token creation, model deployments. logs are stored with integrity controls and we can export via secure syslog/S3 to your account for long-term retention.
7:40 Marcus: retention windows? For compliance we need at least 7 years for certain logs.
8:05 Jonas: Out of the box we keep operational logs for 90 days; we provide log export/archival recommendations and customers typically push to their SIEM for long-term. we can support custom retention via your own S3 bucket or log sink.
8:45 Elena: About evidence — what artifacts will you provide for the SIG?
9:05 Aisha: Typical artifacts: SOC 2 Type II report, control matrix mapping, architecture diagram, network segmentation diagram, sample KMS key policy, vulnerability management policy, pen test summary (redacted), and our incident response runbook (redacted).
9:50 Priya: Can you attach a network diagram that shows where logs live and how keys flow?
10:15 Jonas: yes we'll attach network-diagram.png and kms-key-policy.txt.
10:45 Samir: On the SIG spreadsheet we have a few high-risk questions around data encryption in transit — what ciphers/versions do you support?
11:05 Jonas: We use TLS 1.2+ with recommended ciphers; for internal service-to-service we use mTLS in some Dedicated/private deployments. we'll note that in the SIG answers.
11:45 Marcus: Regarding model data, do you store request/response payloads? we need to know if any customer content is persisted longer than necessary.
12:10 Aisha: By default we persist request metadata for debugging and billing; payload retention is configurable — we can set retention to minimal or disable persistent logging of content for sensitive customers. That will be documented in the SIG.
12:45 Priya: Is there an option to redact PII automatically?
13:05 Jonas: We have tokenization and redaction hooks at the edge, plus customers can configure suppression of raw payloads. We'll discuss patterns in the deep dive.
13:40 Elena: For encryption at rest are DBs and object storage encrypted with CMKs?
14:00 Jonas: Yes, storage is encrypted at rest using AES256 and envelope encryption with KMS-backed keys. Customers can bring their own CMKs for Dedicated and Private.
14:30 Marcus: SSO provisioning — do you support SCIM for automated onboarding/offboarding?
14:50 Jonas: Yes SCIM v2 supported, and SAML 2.0 for login. we can show a sample SCIM mapping.
15:20 Priya: Audit trails — how granular are they? do they include field-level changes?
15:40 Jonas: We include action-level events (create, update, delete) for resources and log which principal made the change; field-level diffs are available in some admin APIs but may require specific entitlement. we'll note that in the SIG.
16:10 Samir: Do you have SOC 2/ISO certifications listed publicly?
16:25 Aisha: SOC 2 Type II is available on request; ISO 27001 currently in progress (expected later this year). we'll send the SOC 2 report and the control mapping.
17:05 Priya: For pen test evidence do you provide full reports or redacted exec summaries?
17:20 Jonas: Typically redacted reports and executive summaries. we can't disclose customer-identifying details.
18:00 Elena: Legal will want a statement on subprocessor list and flow-down obligations.
18:20 Aisha: We'll include our subprocessors list and the standard flow-down language.
18:50 Marcus: Any change management documentation? we need to know how schema/model updates are reviewed and rolled out.
19:10 Jonas: We have release policies, can provide change control process, and can show canary/rollout configs and rollback procedures.
19:50 Priya: Are there built-in rate limits and quotas to prevent noisy neighbor?
20:05 Jonas: yes per-account quotas, we also isolate workloads on Dedicated. we can configure cgroups and GPU pools for stronger isolation on Dedicated/Private.
20:40 Samir: Customers sometimes ask about vendor risk alternatives — who do you commonly see us compare to?
21:05 Aisha: Customers often compare to Anthropic, OpenAI, and self-hosted inference stacks.
21:30 Marcus: ok, on the SIG spreadsheet Q52 we asked about access reviews cadence — what do you recommend?
21:50 Jonas: We recommend quarterly access reviews with role certification; we'll include our recommended cadence and an example report.
22:30 Priya: For the audit logs export, can we ship logs to our AWS account?
22:50 Jonas: yes we can deliver logs to a customer-managed S3 or streaming endpoint (Kinesis/Firehose) with encryption using your CMK.
23:20 Elena: Legal will want to confirm incident notification timelines.
23:40 Aisha: Our policy is 72 hours for breaches with high severity and immediate notification for critical incidents; we'll include the incident response SLAs.
24:10 Marcus: A few SIG answers look like 'see attached artifact' — can you provide those artifacts after the call?
24:35 Aisha: absolutely — SOC 2, network diagram, KMS policy, subprocessors list, and a redacted pen test executive summary.
25:05 Jonas: i'll prepare a short tech appendix showing KMS flow and what changes in Dedicated vs Private.
25:40 Priya: For Private on-prem installs — do you provide an installation checklist and runbook?
26:00 Jonas: yes runbook, infra-as-code templates, and a security checklist. some customers also contract professional services for install.
26:35 Samir: procurement question — what's the SLA for Dedicated?
26:50 Aisha: Dedicated SLA is in the enterprise addendum; typical uptime 99.9 with credits. we'll include the SLA doc.
27:20 Marcus: Data residency — confirm hosted US and EU regions available?
27:40 Aisha: yes US (us-east) and EU (eu-west) deployments available. for other regions we have partners.
28:05 Priya: Do you support egress controls and private endpoints?
28:20 Jonas: yes VPC endpoints and private networking are supported for Private and Dedicated. we'll include example VPC peering diagrams.
28:50 Elena: On the SIG, question about encryption key rotation — what's the cadence and process?
29:10 Jonas: Key rotation policy is annually by default; customers can configure rotation via AWS KMS automatic rotation or manage manually. we'll include key rotation docs.
29:50 Samir: For high-risk questions, we may need RTO/RPO numbers for critical services. do you publish those?
30:10 Aisha: We can provide target RTO/RPO for Dedicated; hosted platform tiers vary. will include in the SLA appendix.
30:45 Priya: Do you perform background checks on employees with access to production?
31:00 Aisha: Yes, we have background screening for roles with production access; will note that and include HR policy excerpts.
31:30 Jonas: ok i'll mark items in the SIG where we need to attach artifacts.
31:50 Marcus: I see a few TODOs on encryption in transit — please be explicit on the cipher suites.
32:10 Jonas: noted. we'll include a cipher suite appendix and TLS config.
32:40 Elena: We'll route internal legal questions to Lina after call.
33:00 Lina: yes I can take that, i'll coordinate contract language and subprocessors answers.
33:25 Samir: timeline — we are trying to close vendor risk process by July 10th.
33:40 Aisha: That seems doable; with artifacts in two weeks and a deep dive we should hit that timeline.
34:10 Priya: can you provide an evidence trail that admin actions are immutable? we need attestation.
34:30 Jonas: We can provide logs and documentation of immutability controls, plus exportable audit trails to your SIEM.
35:00 Marcus: Any privacy-specific docs? data processing agreement?
35:15 Aisha: yes DPA is standard; we'll include a blank DPA and data flow annex.
35:45 Priya: For key custody, will Redwood ever see the decrypted keys?
36:00 Jonas: No — with BYOK the key material remains in your KMS; Redwood uses KMS APIs but does not export key material. we'll include a diagram showing key flow.
36:40 Elena: For the SIG's insurance question, can you provide cyber liability limits?
36:55 Aisha: We'll provide our current cyber insurance summary.
37:20 Samir: about incident postmortems — will you share redacted examples?
37:40 Jonas: Yes executive postmortems are available in redacted form.
38:10 Marcus: Great. let's recap next steps.
38:25 Aisha: Recap — we'll send SIG export, SOC 2 report, network diagram, KMS policy, subprocessors list, redacted pen test summary; Jonas to prep tech appendix and KMS flow; Lina to coordinate contracts/legal. deep dive scheduling week of 6/22.
39:00 Priya: sounds good.
39:20 Aisha: any final Qs?
39:35 Marcus: none, thanks.
39:50 Elena: thanks all.
40:10 Meeting end.

Artifacts referenced: redwood-soc2-2025.pdf (SOC 2 Type II report), redwood-sig-export-2026-06-10.xlsx (completed SIG), network-diagram.png, kms-key-policy.txt, subprocessors-list.csv, pen-test-exec-summary.pdf. Links will be provided by email.

Notes about transcript: occasional word errors (e.g., 'canary' transcribed as 'can I re'), some speaker attribution merged (Jonas/Aisha), natural speech patterns present.
